name: Drug-induced Localized Lipodystrophy
aliases: Localized Lipoatrophy due to Drug Injection

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Drug-induced Localized Lipodystrophy

criteria.description: History of subcutaneous or intramuscular injection of known causative drugs (e.g., corticosteroids, insulin, antibiotics)
Clinically evident localized loss of subcutaneous adipose tissue at injection sites
No evidence of generalized or familial lipodystrophy syndromes
Skin biopsy showing localized adipocyte atrophy with minimal inflammation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of both major criteria and exclusion of systemic lipodystrophy
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Histopathology is supportive but not mandatory; diagnosis is primarily clinical.

imaging: Ultrasound showing localized subcutaneous fat loss without mass lesion
MRI may demonstrate focal lipoatrophy with preserved underlying musculature
other: Histopathology showing adipocyte atrophy with minimal inflammatory infiltrate

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of skin induration and fibrosis
Often idiopathic or associated with autoimmune conditions

redFlags: Rapid progression of fat loss beyond injection sites
Signs of systemic lipodystrophy or metabolic complications
Ulceration or secondary infection at affected site
references: Bolognia JL, Schaffer JV, Cerroni L. Dermatology. 4th ed. Elsevier; 2018.
Kumar P, Clark M. Clinical Medicine. 10th ed. Elsevier; 2020.
